entry.ownership_target: vllm/v1 调度器性能优化 与 csrc/cpu (Apple Silicon) 端侧算子库
entry.why_this_target: 这是在“无本地 GPU”硬约束下最务实且高价值的路径。根据 setup.py，macOS 会强制 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu，这意味着 csrc/cpu 是你唯一能本地编译的 C++ 算子库，你可以借此发挥 Kernel 优化专长，提升 vLLM 在 Mac 上的端侧推理性能。同时，vllm/v1 是纯 Python 实现的下一代核心调度器，当前处于极速迭代期（提交热点），你可以在本地完美运行并进行架构级性能剖析。通过在这两个模块建立声誉，你可以逐步获得维护者信任，后续再通过 CI 和 Colab 介入你擅长的 CUDA (csrc/libtorch_stable) 和 Triton 算子开发。
phase_30: 严格按照 AGENTS.md 要求，使用 uv venv --python 3.12 和 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu uv pip install -e . 在 Mac 上配置本地开发环境。
安装 pre-commit 并确保所有本地提交都带有 DCO sign-off（git commit -s）。
在 Mac 上运行 python -m pytest tests/v1 和 tests/models，确保纯 Python 和 CPU 链路完全跑通。
阅读 csrc/cpu/cpu_attn_neon.hpp 和 csrc/cpu/cpu_fused_moe.cpp，寻找 ARM NEON 向量化指令的优化空间。
阅读 vllm/v1 目录下的调度逻辑，使用 Python profiler 跑一个本地 CPU 推理任务，记录调度开销。
在 GitHub Issue 中搜索带有 'cpu' 或 'v1' 标签的 bug，尝试提交 1-2 个修复 PR。
参与 2-3 个涉及 Triton 或 CUTLASS 算子的 PR Code Review，通过静态分析指出潜在的访存冲突或性能问题，展现你的 Kernel 功底。
phase_60: 为 csrc/cpu 提交一个实质性的性能优化 PR（例如优化 CPU 上的 MoE 路由或 MLA Attention 算子），并在 PR 中附带 Mac 上的 Benchmark 数据。
针对 vllm/v1 调度器，提交一个减少 Python 对象创建或优化 Batching 逻辑的 PR，@bwasti 请求 Review。
在 Colab T4 上配置测试环境，挑选一个 vllm/kernels 下的 Triton 算子进行重构或优化，利用 T4 跑通单测后提交 PR。
跟进 #57589 (DiffusionGemma) 等多模态/DiT 相关的 Issue，利用你的扩散模型经验，协助完善 Python 层的模型接入。
在 PR 描述中严格遵守 AGENTS.md 的规定，清晰声明测试命令、结果以及 AI 辅助情况。
开始在 Slack 社区 (slack.vllm.ai) 的 #development 频道活跃，分享你对 Apple Silicon 端侧推理性能的观察。

盲写一个复杂的 CUDA/CUTLASS 算子优化（如针对 FP8/NVFP4 量化 GEMM），通过 Colab T4 验证正确性，并依赖 CI 完成 A100/H100 的性能回归测试。

向项目组申请 Triage 权限，帮助梳理和打标日益增长的 Issue 列表。
在 vLLM 官方博客 (blog.vllm.ai) 或个人技术博客发表一篇关于《如何在无 GPU 环境下参与顶级大模型推理引擎开发》的文章，扩大影响力。

risks.mitigation: 严格执行 AGENTS.md 中的查重命令：提交前使用 gh issue view 和 gh pr list 搜索相关关键字，确保工作独一无二。

## Environment

- 8× AMD Instinct MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.14.0, amdgpu 6.19.14
- Image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly` (2026-08-12, v0.26.1rc1.dev668+g3ee2df303)
  - plus local backports of #51821 (merged 08-13) and #52058 / #51252 (open) — reproduces identically without the two open-PR backports
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, TP=8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla`,
  `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, attention backend `DEEPSEEK_SPARSE_SWA`

## 🐛 Describe the bug

Needle-in-haystack retrieval works perfectly for short prompts and collapses to 0/3
somewhere between **3,611 tokens (3/3 retrieved)** and **5,294 tokens (0/3)**. Above the
threshold the model claims the needles do not exist and output quality degrades broadly
(often rambling to `max_tokens`). No crash, no error — **healthy server, silently wrong
results**. GSM8K-style short-prompt correctness is unaffected (facts probes pass).

Measured (3 needles at 10%/50%/90% depth, `temperature=0`):

| prompt tokens | retrieved |
|---|---|
| 1,913 | 3/3 |
| 3,611 | 3/3 |
| 5,294 | 0/3 |
| 7,003 / 10,411 / 12,061 / 27k / 84k / 253k / 506k | 0/3 (10,411 once gave 2/3 with a corrupted digit string) |

## Ruled out experimentally

- `max_model_len` (fails identically at 131,072 and 1,048,576)
- chunked-prefill boundary (`max_num_batched_tokens=16384`; 12k prompts are single-chunk and still fail)
- #51252 (sparse-indexer prefill buffer budget) — backported, no change on this path
- AITER `fp8_mqa_logits` split-KV heuristic (`seq_len_kv >= 4096` → splits>1):

issues.title: [Bug] [watermarking]: reference detection server does not support dual_key_gumbel; detector alpha default disagrees with generation default
issues.body:
### Your current environment

N/A — code-level report against current `main` (17e50b9b761023d5f2499f062507df1ff49092a4); no runtime environment involved.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Two related gaps after #56122.

### 1. Reference detection server cannot detect `dual_key_gumbel` output

`examples/basic/online_serving/watermark_detection_server.py` always constructs `GumbelWatermarkDetector` (line 60). Its argparse takes only `--tokenizer / --key / --prf / --context-width / --p-value-threshold`. There is no `--algorithm` or `--alpha`, so text generated with `algorithm="dual_key_gumbel"` cannot be detected with the reference server. `docs/features/watermarking.md` points users at this server as the deployment pattern (line 228). It should accept `--algorithm dual_key_gumbel --alpha <value>` and build `DualKeyGumbelWatermarkDetector`.

### 2. Detector `alpha` default disagrees with generation default

- `DualKeyGumbelWatermarkDetector.__init__` defaults `alpha=0.2` (`vllm/v1/watermarking/gumbel.py:220`)
- `WatermarkConfig.alpha` defaults to `0.1` (`vllm/config/watermarking.py:35`), as does `DualKeyGumbelWatermarker` (`gumbel.py:107`)

The detector uses `alpha` in the variance normalization (`gumbel.py:252`: `variance = (1 - self.alpha) ** 2 + self.alpha ** 2`), so a silent default mismatch changes p-values. Suggest aligning the detector default to 0.1, or dropping the default and requiring `alpha` explicitly.

### Docs nit

Worth a one-line note in the constraints section that `deduplicate_contexts` and speculative decoding are mutually exclusive in effect today. It is stated at `docs/features/watermarking.md:80-82`, but under the spec-decode heading where it is easy to miss.

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

issues.title: [Bug]: fp8 FlashMLA sparse decode crashes at engine init with --enforce-eager on SM90 (dummy-run aten::new_empty dispatch failure, size-dependent)
issues.body:
### Your current environment

```
vLLM       : dev tree at e378275a8 (≈ main mid-Sep 2026) + index-kpool fix,
             rebuilt from source (vllm 0.1.dev427+gb90f0e8fb.cu131)
GPU        : 8 × NVIDIA H100 80GB (SM90), TP=8
Model      : zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration,
             NoPE MLA: kv_lora_rank=512, qk_rope_head_dim=0)
Backend    : FLASHMLA_SPARSE (head_size 512, fp8_ds_mla kv cache)
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Booting with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` (fp8_ds_mla envelope on the FlashMLA
sparse backend, per the NoPE-512 envelope mechanism in PR #55543) plus
`--enforce-eager` crashes during the engine's init dummy run:

```
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashmla_sparse.py:1245, in _fp8_flash_mla_kernel
    out, lse = flash_mla_with_kvcache(...)
vllm/third_party/flashmla/flash_mla_interface.py:175, in flash_mla_with_kvcache
    out, lse, new_tile_scheduler_metadata, new_num_splits = flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd(...)
RuntimeError: torch_call_dispatcher("aten::new_empty", "", stack.data(),
    (((0ULL + 2) << 56) | ((0ULL + 13) << 48) | ((0ULL + 0) << 40) | ((0ULL + 0) << 0)))
API call failed at torch/csrc/stable/ops.h, line 939
```

Call chain: `kernel_warmup()` → `flashinfer_autotune()` →
`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs()` → the fp8 sparse decode kernel.

**Trigger isolation (three arms):**

1. Engine init with `--enforce-eager` at `max_num_batched_tokens=16384` →
   crashes as above.
2. The same engine init at `max_num_batched_tokens=8192` → boots and
   serves fine.
3. Direct eager kernel calls with REAL shapes (same interface, same dtypes,
   outside the dummy-run context) → do NOT crash.

So the trigger is size-dependent and lives in the dummy-run path (a
degenerate batch shape the warmup runs at 16K but not 8K, or a
dummy-run-specific metadata state), not in the fp8 sparse kernel itself.

**What works (control):**
- Same serve with CUDA graphs ON (no `--enforce-eager`): boots, serves,
  passes GSM8K at 0.995 accuracy on this exact envelope path.
- bf16 kv cache (same backend, no fp8_ds_mla): boots fine with
  `--enforce-eager`.

**Minimal repro shape** (from our repro script; happy to attach):

```python
# arm (C) — the crash:
LLM(model="/data/models/glm53flash", kv_cache_dtype="fp8",
    enforce_eager=True, max_num_batched_tokens=16384,
    tensor_parallel_size=8)
# arm (A) — OK: same with max_num_batched_tokens=8192
# arm (B) — OK: direct flash_mla_cuda.sparse_decode_fwd eager calls
#     at real shapes (q=[T,H,576] bf16, 656B fp8_ds_mla cache, topk=128)
```

**Impact:** any SM90 user running `--enforce-eager` with fp8_ds_mla on the
sparse-MLA path hits this at startup. The production graph path is
unaffected.

### Notes

- Our tree carries PR #55543's NoPE-512 envelope port plus small fixes; the
  crash reproduces on the fp8 sparse decode path regardless of the envelope
  shim (it fires inside `sparse_decode_fwd` before any model-specific
  padding is read).
- Suspected classes: degenerate dummy-run shape at ≥16K tokens, or a
  stable-ABI/eager-dispatch edge in `sparse_decode_fwd` (the error is a
  stable-ABI `aten::new_empty` dispatch failure, not a CUDA IMA).
- Happy to run further isolation (specific dummy shapes, other
  max_num_batched_tokens values, nvfp4_ds_mla) on request.

*(AI-assisted reproduction and isolation; every number/log line above was
verified by a human reviewer. Full traceback available on request.)*

issues.title: [Bug]: DeepSeek-V4.1 produces NaN with CUDA graphs on SM120/121 — dummy capture batches poison the null KV block
issues.body:
## Your current environment

```
vLLM            main @ b443c1c (built from source)
FlashInfer      0.6.18.post1
PyTorch         2.13 + CUDA 13.0
GPU             8x NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121), 121.6 GiB unified memory each
OS              Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64
Model           DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP8 + EP8
Backend         FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41
KV cache        fp8_ds_mla, indexer MXFP4, block size 64 (SWA cache 32)
```

## Describe the bug

With CUDA graphs enabled, `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` returns empty or garbled completions.
`--enforce-eager` is correct. All graph modes fail identically: `FULL`, `PIECEWISE`, and
`FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

Eager, correct:

```
prompt: "The capital of France is"   ->  " Paris."
```

PIECEWISE, same build and weights:

```
prompt: "The capital of France is"   ->  ""
```

## Root cause

**Every attention output row is NaN from the first decoder layer onward, while its inputs are
finite.** A replay-time probe on the breakable-CUDA-graph segments shows layer 0 receiving
finite `hidden_states`, `q` and `kv`, then writing NaN into the real-token rows of its output
buffer.

The NaN comes from the KV cache, specifically block 0.

`sparse_mla_sm120/decode_dsv4_kernel.cuh` deliberately gathers slot 0 for invalid indices and
relies on softmax masking to discard it. The scale load is guarded:

```cpp
// line 272
if (idx_raw >= 0) {
  ...
  scale_word = __ldg(...);
}
```

but the NoPE/RoPE data load is not — it clamps instead:

```cpp
// line 299
const int idx = (idx_raw >= 0) ? idx_raw : 0;
const int block_idx_g = idx / section_pbs;
```

The intent is documented at line 431:

> Invalid = position past section_len OR slot id = -1 (indexer-padded; IO already gathered
> slot 0 into smem with idx clamped — masking to -inf kills it in softmax).

Masking sets the logit to `-1e30`, so softmax yields `p ≈ 0`. But the PV accumulation still
computes `p * v`, and in IEEE arithmetic `0 * NaN = NaN`. In MLA the NoPE tensor serves as both
K and V, so non-finite data in slot 0 propagates into `acc_nope` regardless of the mask.

**The kernel therefore has an undocumented precondition: block 0 must hold finite data.**

Measured contents of block 0, same build, immediately before the first real request:

| Mode | slot 0 NoPE | slot 0 RoPE | scales |
|---|---|---|---|
| eager | 0.0 | 0.0 | all zero |
| PIECEWISE | **NaN** | **~3.2e35** | all zero |

CUDA graph capture is what pollutes it. Dummy capture batches carry an all-zero block table,
so writes land in block 0 while the graph is being recorded.

## Reproduction of the causal step

Rather than argue from correlation, I copied the cache and re-ran the same kernel with the same
inputs, changing only block 0:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| E: block 0 as-is | output rows 0-4 NaN |
| F: block 0 zeroed | output finite and correct |

Cloning every input tensor (`q`, `sparse_indices`, `swa_topk_lens`, `sinks`, `out`,
`workspace_buffer`) and re-running reproduced the NaN, which rules out the inputs.

Also ruled out, each tested individually: stream mismatch (`torch.cuda.synchronize()` and
`tvm_ffi.use_torch_stream()` both made no difference), the autotuner's `chunks_per_block`
tactic (tested -1, 1, 2, 3, 8), page-block-size handling, and widening the eager region
(`VLLM_V41_WIDE_EAGER=1`).

## Workaround

Zeroing block 0 before each kernel call fixes it completely. Block 0 is vLLM's reserved
`null_block` (`vllm/v1/core/block_pool.py`, popped at init and never handed to a request), so
this i

issues.title: [RFC]: Data integrity and I/O liveness for the filesystem KV offload tier
issues.body:
### Motivation.

The filesystem secondary tier (`vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/fs/`) is a data path with no integrity verification and no bound on how long a single I/O operation may take. #49328 established the partial-keep contract this builds on: a failed load marks its own cached lookup verdict a miss and reports how many blocks loaded before the failure, so earlier blocks survive. Two gaps remain on top of that:

1. **No data integrity verification.** Block contents written to the filesystem tier are never checksummed. `_load_block` detects a file shorter than `block_size` and deletes it, so truncation is caught. What is not caught is content that is the right length and the wrong bytes: bit rot on the storage device, a partially rewritten file, or a block written by an instance whose layout differs in a way the `FileMapper` path hash does not capture. Such a block is copied into the primary tier and consumed as attention KV, producing wrong logits with no error signal anywhere in the system.

2. **No deadline on filesystem I/O.** `batch_store_block` and `batch_load_block` run as a single pool task per job with no deadline. A stalled NFS mount, hung FUSE filesystem, or a device in error recovery blocks that pool thread indefinitely. The pool is bounded at `n_read_threads` + `n_write_threads` (16 + 16 by default), and read-priority threads fall back to the store queue and vice versa, so ~32 stuck operations stall all tiering traffic in both directions. This is the tier-side half of the problem reported in #49829: that issue bounds how long the scheduler waits on a `HIT_PENDING` block, but nothing bounds the write it is waiting for.

Two smaller gaps follow from the same code path:

1. **Stale temporary files are never reclaimed.** `_store_block` writes to `<dest>_<random>.tmp` and `os.replace` it, cleaning up the temp file if the write raises. If the engine dies between the two (OOM kill, SIGKILL, node preemption), the temp file survives with nothing that will ever remove it. On a long-lived shared PVC these accumulate without bound.

2. **No errno-based error classification.** Both the C and Python I/O paths already surface `errno` (`PyErr_SetFromErrnoWithFilename` in `csrc/fs_io.cpp`), and partial progress is already reported (`exc.num_succeeded` -> `JobResult.successful_keys`, added in #49328). Nothing consumes the errno. A transient `ESTALE` on an NFS remount is treated identically to a permanent `ENOSPC`: the remaining keys in the batch are marked a miss and recomputed.

These matter most on shared or network filesystems (NFS, POSIX PVCs), which the tier explicitly supports: `FileSystemTierManager` documents cross-instance cache sharing over a common `root_dir`.

### Proposed Change.

Four changes, each independently. Every one of them touches both I/O implementations: `vllm/v1/kv_offload/tiering/fs/io.py` is a pure-Python fallback, and `csrc/fs_io.cpp` (built as `vllm.fs_io_C`) is the path actually taken whenever the extension imports. 

### 1. Block-level checksum validation
**What:** Compute a CRC32C over each block when storing it to the filesystem tier, persist it with the block, and verify it on load. A mismatch deletes the file and marks the key a miss rather than returning corrupt KV.
**Design:**
- **Placement, given O_DIRECT.** The tier prefers `O_DIRECT` and falls back to buffered I/O only where the probe fails, so block payloads must stay length- and offset-aligned. A 4-byte trailer appended to the payload breaks that a

### 🐛 Describe the bug

# Out-of-bounds `attrIdxs` in the C++ batch memcpy path (`cache_kernels.cu`)

## Summary

The C++ batch-copy path in `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu` passes a **single** `size_t` as the `attrIdxs` array to `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` / `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`, regardless of the descriptor count — the same contract violation fixed for the Python path in vllm-project/vllm#53860.

The CUDA Driver API documentation for `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` specifies `attrIdxs` as an array of `count` elements (indices into `attrs`, each `< numAttrs`). Passing `&attrs_idx` where `attrs_idx` is one stack scalar while `count` is large (typically thousands of 64 KiB KV blocks per offload) leaves the driver reading past the end of that scalar — an out-of-bounds read / undefined behavior that currently happens to work only because adjacent stack bytes happen to read as tolerable values.

## Location

Two sites, both in the batch-copy helper (around L130–L230 of `csrc/libtorch_stable/cache_kernels.cu`):

**CUDA path (L169):**
```cpp
size_t attrs_idx = 0;
size_t fail_idx = 0;
...
CUresult result = batch_fn(..., static_cast<size_t>(cnt), &attr, &attrs_idx, 1,
                           &fail_idx, static_cast<CUstream>(stream));
```

**ROCm path (L196):** the same `size_t attrs_idx = 0;`

issues.title: [Bug]: A weight update issued while the engine is asleep segfaults the EngineCore instead of being rejected
issues.body:
### Your current environment

vLLM main (c3b4844, 2026-09-19), torch 2.13.0+cu130, one RTX 6000 Ada (sm_89), Linux. Model `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`, `--enable-sleep-mode`, `--weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "ipc"}'`, `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1`. Reproduces with the default CUDA graphs, with `--enforce-eager`, and with ngram speculative decoding.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

If the trainer sends a weight update after `sleep()` and before `wake_up()`, the worker copies the new tensors into weight memory that the CuMemAllocator has unmapped, and the EngineCore dies with a segfault in the device copy:

```
POST /sleep?level=1                         -> 200
POST /start_weight_update                   -> 200
POST /update_weights   (CUDA IPC payload)   -> never returns
!!!!!!! Segfault encountered !!!!!!!
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in cuMemcpyDtoDAsync_v2
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in cudaMemcpyAsync
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in at::native::copy_device_to_device(at::TensorIterator&, bool, bool)
  ...
  File "<unknown>", line 0, in torch::autograd::THPVariable_copy_(_object*, _object*, _object*)
(APIServer) WARNING [core_client.py:803] [shutdown] MPClient: engine core exited unexpectedly; starting cleanup
(APIServer) ERROR [async_llm.py:858] vllm.v1.engine.exceptions.EngineDeadError
```

The API server stays up, every later request fails with `EngineDeadError`, and the trainer only sees its `/update_weights` call time out. Nothing in the control plane refuses the update: `start_weight_update` returns 200 while the weights are unmapped, and the worker's `update_weights` goes straight to `model.load_weights`, i.e. `param.data.copy_(...)` into the unmapped range.

Minimal reproduction, following `examples/rl/rlhf_http_ipc.py` with one extra call:

```python
# server: vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-sleep-mode --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "ipc"}' \
#           --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --port 8000   (VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_ALLOW_INSECURE_SERIALIZATION=1)
import requests, torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer import HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient, ModuleSource, WeightTransferTrainerFactory
from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.ipc_engine import IPCTrainerInitInfo

base = "http://localhost:8000"
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B", dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda:0")
engine = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
    init_info=IPCTrainerInitInfo(rank=0, packed=False),
    client=HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient(base), source=ModuleSource(model))
requests.post(f"{base}/sleep", params={"level": "1"}).raise_for_status()
engine.send_weights()   # start_weight_update -> 200, update_weights -> engine segfaults
```

The same sequence with `wake_up()` before `send_weights()` works and leaves every parameter bit-identical to a fresh load, so this is only about the missing guard, not the transfer itself. The documented RL transaction in #48310 is pause → sleep → wake(weights) → update, so the update should be refused with a clear error while `weights` is still asleep (including after a partial `wake_up(tags=["kv_cache"])`), the way `release_kv_cache_memory()` already refuses when executor memory is not resident.

issues.title: [Bug]: DecodeBenchConnector repeats KV cache fills for shared state tensors at large batch sizes
issues.body:
### Your current environment

<details>

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (x86_64)
- Python: 3.12.3
- vLLM: 0.25.1
- PyTorch: 2.12.1
- Engine: vLLM V1
- KV connector: DecodeBenchConnector
- Execution backend: Multiprocessing
- Workload: Long-context decode benchmark with a large batch size (256 requests)
- KV cache layout: Hybrid KV cache with shared state tensors


</details>


### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug Description

`DecodeBenchConnectorWorker.start_fill_kv()` currently processes requests one by one and fills the KV cache separately for each request.

For hybrid KV cache layouts, multiple requests may reference the same state tensor. The current implementation fills the same state tensor repeatedly for every request.

Block-indexed KV cache entries are also filled per request, even when block IDs overlap across requests.

As the batch size increases, the repeated fill operations introduce significant overhead before the first decode step.

In our vLLM-MLU testing environment, this behavior was observed during large-batch, long-context decode benchmarks and was associated with worker RPC timeouts.

The repeated-fill behavior can be identified in the upstream `DecodeBenchConnector` implementation. However, the runtime timeout has so far been reproduced on the MLU backend.

## Reproduction

The issue was observed with the following configuration:

- Engine: vLLM V1
- KV connector: `DecodeBenchConnector`
- KV cache layout: Hybrid KV cache containing shared state tensors
- Batch size: 256
- Execution backend: Multiprocessing
- Workload: Long-context decode benchmark

The issue occurs during the initial KV cache fill before the first decode step.

Instrumentation of `start_fill_kv()` shows that shared state tensors are filled repeatedly across requests within a single invocation.

As the number of requests increases, the repeated fill operations can significantly increase the initialization time.

## Actual Behavior

The initial KV cache fill becomes increasingly expensive at large batch sizes.

In our testing environment, the excessive delay was associated with the following errors:

```text
TimeoutError: RPC call to sample_tokens timed out No available shared memory broadcast block found
```

A subsequent error while querying worker memory usage may occur after the worker RPC has already timed out.

The repeated state-tensor fills occur before the first decode step.

## Expected Behavior

`start_fill_kv()` should avoid filling the same shared state tensor more than once within a single invocation.

Block IDs should be merged and deduplicated per KV cache group before the fill operation.

The implementation should also avoid creating a full-batch temporary value tensor when filling a large number of blocks.

These changes should reduce redundant KV cache initialization work without changing the intended cache contents.

## Related Pull Request

This issue is related to PR #56473:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56473

That PR discusses reducing temporary tensor allocation and fill overhead in `DecodeBenchConnector`.

## Temporary Workaround

A backend-specific workaround currently:

- Merges block IDs by KV cache group.
- Deduplicates block IDs.
- Deduplicates shared state tensors by object identity.
- Fills contiguous block ranges in place.
- Uses indexed writes for sparse blocks.

The workaround reduces redundant operations during the initial KV cache fill.

It can be removed once an equivalent upstream fix is merged and included

issues.title: [Feature]: Support multi-turn conversation for OpenAI Response API
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

I wanted to test **GPT-OSS-120B** served via **vLLM** using AI coding agents such as **opencode** and **codex**.
For these agents, **tool calling and multi-turn conversations are essential**, and according to OpenAI's documentation, the **`/v1/responses` endpoint** is the recommended API for this use case.

#### Observed behavior

When configuring both agents (opencode and codex) to call the model through the **`/v1/responses` endpoint**, everything works smoothly for the **first request**:
vLLM responds correctly and returns a valid output.

However, when continuing the conversation (**multi-turn interaction**), at the very second request, vLLM fails and returns **validation errors**.

The failure seems to occur because these agents send the conversation history using the **OpenAI Responses API format**, which vLLM does **not currently support**.

vLLM expects inputs formatted according to the **Chat Completions API**:

```json
{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hi there!"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "How are you?"}
  ]
}
```

The agents send requests using the **Responses API format**:

```json
{
  "input": [
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "Hello" }]
    },
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": [{ "type": "output_text", "text": "Hi there!" }]
    },
    {
      "type": "reasoning",
      "encrypted_content": null,
      "summary": []
    },
    {
      "type": "message",
      "role": "user",
      "content": [{ "type": "input_text", "text": "How are you?" }]
    }
  ]
}
```

Error returned by vLLM:

```
400 Bad Request: 356 validation errors
- Input should be a valid string
- Field required: ResponseReasoningItem.id
- Field required: ResponseOutputMessage.id
- ...
```


#### Question / Feature request

Are there plans to support the **OpenAI Responses API** in vLLM?
This would enable proper **multi-turn conversations and tool-calling workflows** for AI agents such as **opencode**, **codex**, and potentially others that rely on this API.


### Steps to reproduce

| Agent    | Version | Command                                                                                                    | Result                                   |
| -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| opencode | v1.1.31 | `opencode run "Hello, this is my first test message."`                                                     | ✅ Success — `"Hello! Nice to meet you."` |
| opencode | v1.1.31 | `opencode run --continue "This is my second message. What was my first message about?"`                    | ❌ 348 validation errors                  |
| codex    | v0.88.0 | `VLLM_API_KEY=test codex exec "Hello, this is my first test message."`                                     | ✅ Success — `"Hello! 👋"`                |
| codex    | v0.88.0 | `VLLM_API_KEY=test codex exec resume --last "This is my second message. What was my first message about?"` | ❌ 356 validation errors                  |


I attached:

* The command used to launch the vLLM server:
```
docker run -d \
  --name vllm \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  --runtime nvidia \
  -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  -v huggingface-cache:/root/.cach

issues.body:
### Your current environment

Single AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (gfx1201, RDNA4), host kernel 7.0.0-31, ROCm 7.2.3 / ROCm 10 depending on the image under test. Models are FP8 compressed-tensors checkpoints (gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic, Qwen3-14B-FP8). Serving with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Writing the process out in detail so it is clear which parts are measured and which are inference.

On RDNA4, `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` starts being selected for `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8` from v0.28.0, and it is slower than the `ChannelWise` kernel that v0.27.1 picks on the same hardware and the same checkpoint.

**v0.27.1 and earlier do not have the problem.** `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported` rejects RDNA4 there (it reports needing CDNA3+ / compute capability 94+), so `ChannelWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` is chosen automatically. We confirmed this in the startup logs of AMD's ROCm 10 image built on 0.27.1.dev.

**From v0.28.0 the gate opens** and the startup log shows:

```
INFO [__init__.py:720] Selected RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8
```

**Causal evidence, v0.28.0, gemma-4-12B-it-FP8-Dynamic, same image, same serve command:**

| | decode tok/s |
|---|---|
| stock v0.28.0 (RowWise selected) | 32.22 (32.20–32.24) |
| same image, RowWise entry removed from the ROCm FP8 kernel list → ChannelWise selected | **35.45 (35.44–35.46)** |

That is +10.0% from removing one entry, with nothing else changed. Run-to-run spread inside each arm is 0.02–0.04 tok/s, so the gap is far outside noise. For reference our v0.23.0 baseline on the same model and card is 33.8, so stock v0.28 is a 4.8% regression against the version we were running.

**v0.29.0 is worse.** Same model and card, RowWise selected: decode **26.16**, against 34.28 on our v0.23.0 baseline — a 24% drop. Removing the RowWise entry recovers it to 28.66 (+9.6%, confirming the same cause is present), but that is still 16% below both v0.23.0 and the AMD 0.27.1 image. So there appears to be a **second, separate regression in 0.29** on top of this one, which we have not isolated; our component comparison ruled out ROCm and torch 2.12, leaving the vLLM 0.29 snapshot or triton 3.7.1 as candidates. Prefill is unaffected in both versions (4116 tok/s on 0.29), which is consistent with the damage being confined to the FP8 linear path rather than attention.

Caveat on the 0.29 numbers: those are one spawn per arm, unlike the 0.28 numbers. The within-run spread was tight (28.59–28.72) and the gap is 16%, so we do not expect the sign to flip, but they are weaker evidence than the 0.28 pair.

### How to reproduce

1. Serve an FP8 compressed-tensors model on gfx1201 with vLLM 0.28.0 or later.
2. Check the startup log for `Selected RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`.
3. Measure decode throughput.
4. Remove `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` from the ROCm FP8 entry in `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py` so `ChannelWise` is chosen, and measure again.

Note that `--linear-backend=torch` cannot be used to isolate this, because it includes all three torch kernels; a source edit is the only way we found to separate them.

### Suggested fix

Either restore the RDNA4 exclusion in `RowWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported`, or order `ChannelWiseTorchFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` ahead of it for RDNA4 specifically. We do not know whether RowWise is a win on CDNA — it may well be, and th

issues.title: [Feature]: [WideEP][CPU]: Add a CPU-only Wide Expert Parallelism well-lit path
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

Add functional Expert Parallelism (EP), including DP-attention + EP-MoE deployments, to the vLLM CPU backend.

The CPU backend currently appears to partially wire up Expert Parallelism, but the default CPU all-to-all path cannot complete because the variable-size collectives required by `AgRsAll2AllManager` are not implemented by `CpuCommunicator`.

The goal is to support CPU-only MoE deployments across multiple ranks/nodes, including use cases such as llm-d Wide Expert Parallelism on x86_64 servers.

This does **not** require porting DeepEP to CPU. A functional CPU communication backend using `torch.distributed`, Gloo, oneCCL, or another appropriate CPU transport would be sufficient as an initial implementation.

### Current implementation

`CpuCommunicator` already detects EP/all-to-all usage and selects the generic `AgRsAll2AllManager`:

```python
if self.use_all2all:
    ...
    from .all2all import AgRsAll2AllManager
    self.all2all_manager = AgRsAll2AllManager(self.cpu_group)
```

GPU-specific all-to-all backends are also explicitly rejected/fallen back to `allgather_reducescatter` on CPU.

However, `AgRsAll2AllManager` requires variable-size collectives:

```python
gathered_tensors = dist_group.all_gatherv(
    tensors_to_gather,
    dim=0,
    sizes=sizes,
)
```

for dispatch, and:

```python
hidden_states = dist_group.reduce_scatterv(
    hidden_states,
    dim=0,
    sizes=sizes,
)
```

for combine.

`CpuCommunicator` currently implements regular `all_gather()`, but does not override `all_gatherv()` or `reduce_scatterv()`.

The implementations inherited from `DeviceCommunicatorBase` raise `NotImplementedError`.

As a result, the CPU backend appears to have the EP/AgRs plumbing in place, but no functional implementation of the communication primitives required for DP+EP execution.

### Desired behavior

`--enable-expert-parallel` should work with the CPU backend using the `allgather_reducescatter` backend, initially without requiring EPLB.

It would be useful to support:

* CPU implementation of `all_gatherv()` and `reduce_scatterv()`, or an alternative CPU-compatible all-to-all implementation.
* Single-node multi-rank CPU EP.
* Multi-node CPU DP+EP.
* MoE expert weights sharded across EP ranks while attention remains data parallel when TP=1.
* A CPU CI test exercising DP > 1 together with `--enable-expert-parallel`.
* Documentation identifying the supported CPU communication backend and expected network requirements.

Dynamic EPLB can remain a separate feature; currently EPLB explicitly rejects CPU platforms.

### Use case

Large MoE models can benefit substantially from expert sharding on CPU servers because the full expert weight set may otherwise exceed the memory capacity or useful memory bandwidth of a single machine.

For example, a cluster of modern x86_64 servers could use:

```text
TP = 1
DP = N
EP = N
```

with attention replicated/data-parallel across the ranks while MoE experts are distributed across the CPU nodes.

This is also the execution model required to provide a CPU variant of llm-d's Wide Expert Parallelism deployment pattern.

### Relevant code

* `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cpu_communicator.py`

  * selects `AgRsAll2AllManager`
  * implements `all_gather()`
  * does not implement `all_gatherv()` / `reduce_scatterv()`
* `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/all2all.py`

  * `AgRsAll2AllManager.dispatch()` uses `all_gatherv()`
  * `AgRsAll2AllManager.co

issues.title: [Bug]: CUTLASS FP8 linear kernel is selected on Ampere while the SM80 dispatch is INT8-only
issues.body:
# [Bug]: CUTLASS FP8 linear kernel is selected on Ampere while the SM80 dispatch is INT8-only

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA A100 (SM80), 32 GPUs
- vLLM: `0.28.1rc1.dev130+g44fe2a392`
- vLLM commit: `44fe2a392b71d52a8d72faf2f8278834379482c9`
- Container digest: `sha256:1ea24ab460278255a2d058667f5f6e67f17bc135180388094dad258543543b0c`
- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4`, revision `395f50b783c6b257e15991d4ed2d24a930a5d0f1`
- Execution: compiled mode with full and piecewise CUDA graphs; `enforce_eager=False`

The complete `collect_env.py` output can be added before submission.

## Describe the bug

### Reproduction

Run inside a pre-initialized 32-GPU multi-node launcher:

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4 \
  --served-model-name Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-NVFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --linear-backend auto \
  --moe-backend auto \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --tensor-parallel-size 16 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --max-num-seqs 64 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --max-model-len 2200 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --block-size 128 \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8,16,32,64],"inductor_compile_config":{"enable_auto_functionalized_v2":true}}'
```

Omission of `--enforce-eager` is intentional. The failure occurs during the compiled profile run before readiness.

With automatic linear-backend selection on A100, vLLM selects:

```text
Selected CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel for ModelOptFp8LinearMethod
```

The engine then fails during the compiled profile run:

```text
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py", line 554, in determine_available_memory
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 857, in profile_run
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 743, in _dummy_run
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 1761, in execute_model
File ".../inductor_cache/...py", line 654, in call
  torch.ops._C.cutlass_scaled_mm.default(buf7, buf6, arg5_1, arg4_1, arg6_1, None)
RuntimeError: cutlass_scaled_mm_sm80_epilogue, /workspace/csrc/libtorch_stable/quantization/w8a8/cutlass/scaled_mm_c2x.cu:89
```

The failure is deterministic on SM80. `CutlassFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel.is_supported()` currently returns true for every CUDA device, causing selection ahead of Marlin. The FP8 linear path supplies E4M3 activations and E4M3 weights, but the SM80 C2x entry requires both operands to be `ScalarType::Char` and instantiates `cutlass_gemm_sm80_dispatch<int8_t, ...>`.

### Passing workaround

The same invocation passes on A100 after changing only the linear backend:

```bash
--linear-backend marlin
```

The passing control selected `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel`, loaded the checkpoint, completed `torch.compile`, captured full and piecewise CUDA graphs, reached readiness, and scored 8/8 on the five-shot GSM8K smoke test with zero invalid answers.

### Fixed by

- vLLM pull request: [#53376 — Gate CUTLASS FP8 linear kernel on SM89+](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53376)
- Required in conjunction on the tested compiled path: [PyTorch #189530 — Fix `auto_functionalized_v2` assertion error with E8M0 inputs](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/189530)

### Expected behavior

Automatic backend selec

issues.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM: `0.29.1rc1.dev47+gdc36fcce9` (nightly build, official Docker image), OpenAI-compatible server
- Python 3.12, pydantic 2.13.x (inside the image)
- Model / tokenizer: DeepSeek-V4.1 (`tokenizers/deepseek_v41.py`, rendered through `DeepseekV4Renderer`)

Full `collect_env.py` output omitted on purpose: the failure happens in request validation / chat-template preprocessing of `/tokenize`, before anything touches the engine, so it is independent of hardware. I also checked the current `main` branch and the relevant code is unchanged (details below).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`POST /tokenize` (chat form) returns **400** for a perfectly ordinary OpenAI-style tool round trip — an assistant message with `"content": null` plus `tool_calls` — while `POST /v1/chat/completions` accepts the *identical* messages and runs fine. `content: null` + `tool_calls` is what the OpenAI SDK and most agent frameworks emit for tool-call turns, so in practice `/tokenize` is unusable for agentic conversations with this tokenizer.

**Minimal reproduction**

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8000/tokenize -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages": [
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is the weather in Shanghai tomorrow?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": null,
     "tool_calls": [{"id": "call_1", "type": "function",
                     "function": {"name": "lookup_weather", "arguments": "{\"city\": \"Shanghai\"}"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": "call_1", "content": "{\"temp_c\": 24, \"condition\": \"cloudy\"}"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Do I need an umbrella?"}
  ],
  "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "lookup_weather",
             "description": "Look up the weather for a city.",
             "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["city"]}}}]
}'
```

Actual:

```json
{"error": {"message": "cannot pickle 'pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidatorIterator' object", "type": "BadRequestError", "param": null, "code": 400}}
```

Expected: `200` with a token count, the same prompt that `/v1/chat/completions` renders for these messages.

Observations from the same server; only the assistant message changes:

| assistant message | `/tokenize` |
|---|---|
| `"content": null` + `tool_calls` | **400** (error above) |
| `"content": ""` + `tool_calls` | 200, `count=372` |
| `content` key omitted + `tool_calls` | 200, `count=372` |
| `"content": null`, no `tool_calls` | 200 |

With an equivalent synthetic conversation (different text) I also sent each variant to `/v1/chat/completions` with `max_tokens=1`: the `content: null` variant is accepted there (200), and `usage.prompt_tokens` was identical for all three variants and equal to the `/tokenize` count of the two variants that work. So rendering is consistent between the two endpoints; only the `null` case is rejected by `/tokenize`.

**Root cause (from reading the code)**

1. `ChatCompletionMessageParam` is a union of the OpenAI SDK TypedDicts and `CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`. The custom type declares `content: str | list[...]` (no `None`) and `tool_calls: list[...] | None`; the OpenAI assistant type allows `content:

issues.title: [Bug]: minimax_m2 / glm47_moe / deepseek_v4 arg converters drop the last parameter when the model omits the closing tag (same class as #57699)
issues.body:
### Your current environment

- vLLM main (probed 2026-09-20; minimax_m2.py @ 24bfbd5d, deepseek_v4.py @ 39e33db7)
- Parser-only bug: reproduction needs no GPU, no model, no server.

### Describe the bug

#57699 describes a bug class for qwen3: when the model closes the tool call **without closing the last parameter tag**, the trailing value is dropped by the final (partial=False) conversion. #57707 fixes qwen3 only - but the same structure exists in three other converters, none of which are covered by that PR:

**1. minimax_m2 - vllm/parser/minimax_m2.py `_minimax_m2_arg_converter`**

`_PARAM_RE` only ends a value at the closing parameter tag or at the next parameter open tag. The trailing `_PARTIAL_PARAM_RE` extraction runs only under `if partial:`, so the final conversion drops the last parameter. With `stream_arg_deltas=True`, the streamed partial conversions have already emitted the value, and the flush at tool-call end produces a shorter JSON - the same client-visible divergence as #57699.

Model output:

```
<minimax:tool_call><invoke name="get_weather">
<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>
<parameter name="unit">celsius
</invoke></minimax:tool_call>
```

non-streaming: `arguments == {"city": "Seattle"}` - `unit` is silently lost.

**2. glm47_moe - vllm/parser/glm47_moe.py `_glm47_arg_converter`**

`_ARG_RE` requires the value close tag; the `_PARTIAL_ARG_RE` extraction is under `if partial:`. `stream_arg_deltas=True` is set. Same divergence: a tool call that omits the last closing arg_value tag yields non-streaming `arguments` without the trailing parameter.

**3. deepseek_v4 (inherited by v32/v41) - vllm/parser/deepseek_v4.py `_dsml_arg_converter`**

Same `if partial:` structure. Additionally, the partial branch swallows JSON failures with `contextlib.suppress` and **drops the value entirely**, while the complete branch falls back to the literal text. So a trailing `string="false"` parameter whose partial value is not yet valid JSON is discarded even mid-stream.

### Reproduction (CPU only)

```python
from vllm.parser.minimax_m2 import _minimax_m2_arg_converter

raw = '<parameter name="city">Seattle</parameter>\n<parameter name="unit">celsius\n'
print(_minimax_m2_arg_converter(raw, partial=True))   # {"city": "Seattle", "unit": "celsius\n"}
print(_minimax_m2_arg_converter(raw, partial=False))  # {"city": "Seattle"}  <- unit dropped
```

Equivalent direct calls to `_glm47_arg_converter` (glm47_moe) and `_dsml_arg_converter` (deepseek_v4) show the same drop.

### Expected behavior

Mirror the qwen3 fix (#57707): the trailing-partial extraction should also run in the final conversion, so a properly closed tool call keeps its last parameter value. For deepseek_v4, the partial branch should also fall back to the literal text like the complete branch does.

I can send PRs (one per parser, following the fix shape of #57707) with regression tests mirroring TestUnclosedLastParameter in tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3.py.

issues.title: [Security]: remote media URLs allow SSRF to internal/link-local addresses by default
issues.body:
Hi team — found this while looking at how the server fetches remote media, and wanted to report it with a fix offer. Verified against `main` (`961c5b6` era tree, re-checked today).

### Problem

On a default setup, the media connector fetches **any** `http(s)` URL it is given — including loopback, link-local, and internal addresses. Three compounding facts:

1. **No domain restriction by default.** `allowed_media_domains` defaults to `None` (`vllm/config/model.py:201`), the connector coerces it to `[]` (`vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py:200-202`), and `_assert_url_in_allowed_media_domains` skips the check entirely when the list is empty (`connector.py:354-364`). So out of the box, any hostname passes.
2. **No IP-based guard anywhere on this path.** I searched `vllm/multimodal/` and the serve tree for private/loopback/link-local denylists (`is_private`, `ip_address`, blocklists) — nothing. A URL pointing at `169.254.169.254` or an internal hostname is fetched as-is.
3. **Redirects are followed by default.** `VLLM_MEDIA_URL_ALLOW_REDIRECTS` defaults to `True` (`vllm/envs.py:79`), threaded through `load_from_url` (`connector.py:391,444`) into `connections.py:get_bytes/async_get_bytes` (`vllm/connections.py:403-445`). An innocent-looking URL can redirect somewhere internal, and the redirect target is never re-checked.

The fetch is server-side, triggered during normal multimodal request processing (`fetch_image` → `MediaConnector(...).fetch_image(image_url)` in `vllm/multimodal/utils.py:367-371`).

### Impact

This is reachable **without an API key on default `vllm serve`**: unauthenticated entry points like `/invocations` route generate-task payloads — including `image_url` — through the same inference path, and the endpoint sits outside all `GUARDED_PREFIX`es. So against any default deployment serving a multimodal model:

```json
{"image_url": {"url": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/"}}
```

is fetched by the serving host itself — cloud-metadata theft and internal-network probing from the server. Fetch timeouts (5s image / 30s video) bound the hang but don't restrict *where* the request goes. To be clear on scope: `file://` URLs are fine by default (they require `--allowed-local-media-path`), and I'm not reporting an auth bypass in `--api-key` itself — this is about the absence of any default restriction on the fetch *destination*.

### Solution

Deny loopback, link-local, and private/reserved IP ranges in the media connector by default — resolved post-DNS and re-checked after each redirect — with an env opt-out (e.g. `VLLM_MEDIA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_IPS`) for setups that genuinely serve media from internal hosts. Optionally surface `--allowed-media-domains` more prominently in the docs alongside it.

### Why this approach

- Default-deny on non-public IPs closes the metadata-service vector completely, even for operators who never set `allowed_media_domains`.
- Checking post-DNS (not just the hostname string) defeats DNS-rebinding-style bypasses where a public hostname resolves internally.
- The opt-out keeps air-gapped/internal-media deployments working with one explicit flag.

### Non-goals

- Not touching `file://` handling (already gated) or fetch timeouts (already exist).
- Not proposing auth changes to `/invocations` or `--api-key` scoping — separate discussion.

### Environment

vLLM `main` (serving tree + `vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py`, `vllm/connections.py`, `vllm/config/model.py`, `vllm/envs.py` as cited above). No cod

issues.body:
### Motivation.

vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py has grown and supports too many kernels at this point. Each has diverse set of features, [standard attention support matrix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/design/attention_backends.md#standard-attention-mha-mqa-gqa-backends) captures the support. 

However, we still have variety of backends within each of these wrappers, that make it too complex to add any new features. 

Broadly, these are the supported features from native flashinfer `BatchPrefill*Wrapper` & `*BatchDecode*Wrapper` api. Note that this api also exposes the trtllm_batch* api when `trtllm-gen` backend is supported. 

  | FlashInfer Prefill API / backend | Arch | FP8 compute | FP8 KV | SWA | NVFP4 KV | LSE return |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, `auto` (routes to fa2 or fa3) | SM80, SM90, SM100 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
  | `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, `fa3` | SM90 | Yes | Yes, only if Q is FP8 | Yes | No | Yes |
  | `BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, `trtllm-gen` | SM100, SM103 | Yes | Yes | Causal: Yes; Non-causal + SWA: No | Yes | Yes |
  | `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, `auto` | SM80, SM90, SM100 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
  | `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, `fa2` | SM80, SM90, SM100 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
  | `BatchPrefillWithRaggedKVCacheWrapper`, `cutlass` |  SM100, SM110 | Yes | Yes | Yes | No | Yes |

And for decode - 
 
  | FlashInfer API / backend | Arch | FP8 compute | FP8 KV | SWA | NVFP4 KV | LSE return |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, `auto/fa2` tensor-core | SM80, SM90, SM100 | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
  | `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, `fa3` | SM90 | Yes | Yes, only if Q is FP8 | Yes, if FA3 checks pass | No | Yes |
  | `BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper`, `trtllm-gen` | SM100, SM103 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |

For the standard FlashInfer prefill/decode wrapper paths, backend="auto" resolves to FA3 when FA3 eligibility checks pass, otherwise FA2. It does not auto-select cuDNN, cutlass, cute-dsl, or trtllm-gen. Also note that NVFP4 KV Cache support for attention kernels is available for backend=`fa2` or backend=`trtllm-gen`. In the current code, we only wire through `trtllm-gen`.  When fa2 backend is selected for nvfp4 kv cache, kv is dequantized to `bfloat16` or `float16` for attention compute. This is in place for NVFP4 compatibility with pre-blackwell from flashinfer 0.6.13 and currently not supported through vLLM.


For the trtllm-gen api, the support matrix looks similar to the selected `trtllm-gen` backend.

issues.title: [RFC]: Expert-granular MoE residency — drive UVA offload from EPLB's per-expert load statistics
issues.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM can already offload MoE expert weights to host memory, and it already knows which experts are hot. It cannot yet use the second fact to drive the first.

What exists on `main` today:

* `PrefetchOffloadConfig.offload_group_size` / `offload_num_in_group` — choose **which layers** to offload.
* `UVAOffloadConfig.cpu_offload_params` — choose **which parameters** to offload, by name segment. Its own docstring uses `"mlp.experts.w2_weight"` as the example.
* `offload_backend="uva"`, with `is_uva_available()` and `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor()` — zero-copy access to pinned host memory.
* `EPLBConfig.window_size` / `step_interval` and EPLB's `expert_load_window` — a rolling record of **observed per-expert load**, already used to periodically rearrange expert *placement* across ranks.

The gap is that `cpu_offload_params` matches whole tensors. It moves `w2_weight` for *all* experts in a layer, or none of them. There is no way to express "this fraction of experts is cold under current traffic; demote them and keep the rest resident", even though the statistics that identify them are already being collected, and the cadence for acting on them already exists.

For a wide-MoE model this is the difference between offload being unusable and being the thing that makes the model fit. Expert weights dominate, routing is heavily skewed in practice, and the cold tail is large and fairly stable over a window. Offloading whole expert tensors costs far too much; offloading the cold tail costs comparatively little and frees VRAM that is worth more as KV cache.

### Proposed Change.

Reuse EPLB's existing loop. It already answers "which experts are cold" and "when do we act on that". This proposal adds only "and therefore where does each expert live".

**1. A fraction, not a count.** One knob:

```
cold_expert_fraction: float = 0.0   # 0.0 disables; e.g. 0.15
```

Per layer, `n_cold = floor(num_local_experts * cold_expert_fraction)`, so it is model- and TP-independent. A raw count is deliberately not offered — it does not transfer across models, and it is the kind of number that ends up hardcoded in a deployment and silently wrong after a reshard.

**2. Residency derived from the load window, on the existing cadence.** At each EPLB rebalance step, rank experts by `expert_load_window` and mark the coldest `n_cold` per layer as host-resident; the rest stay device-resident. This is deliberately the *same* trigger and the *same* data EPLB already uses to rearrange placement — residency rebalance alongside placement rebalance, not a second scheduler.

Between rebalance steps the split is **static**. That is the point; see rejected alternatives.

**3. A two-bank forward.** Run the stock expert forward once over the device bank and once over the host bank, and sum. Two `expert_map`s. Router top-k computed once and reused. Shared experts added on the device call only, so they are not double-counted.

**4. Correct split ordering.** The split must happen *after* `process_weights_after_loading`, because the weights must already carry the quant method's real repacked layout. The kernel/config must be rebuilt for **both** banks — one config shared across two banks silently runs cold weights against hot scales, which does not crash and produces plausible wrong output. This was a real bug we hit.

**5. The ranking policy is a hook.** `expert_load_window` is the default input, but the selection itself should be pluggable so deployments can subs

issues.title: [Feature]: Fast Start For vLLM
issues.body:
## Overview

Fast Start reduces vLLM startup time by avoiding repeated checkpoint loading, weight processing, and kernel autotuning during engine restarts and scaling events.

The core design uses a persistent per-GPU weight daemon. The daemon loads and processes model weights once, keeps sharded weights in GPU memory, and exposes them to new vLLM engines through CUDA IPC or a multi-node transport.

When a compatible cache is unavailable, vLLM falls back to the existing checkpoint loader.

## Design Goals

- Reuse processed GPU weights across engine instances.
- Support TP, PP, EP, multi-node deployments, and MTP.
- Support quantized formats including FP8 and FP4.
- Cache autotune results with hardware- and version-aware keys.
- Preserve correctness through strict cache validation.
- Provide a reliable fallback path for cache misses and failures.

## Cache Validation

# [RFC] LoRA Adapter Lifecycle for RL Training

## Problem

RL + LoRA workflows have three vLLM-side issues:

1. **sleep/wake crash**: Level-2 sleep with `enable_lora=True` crashes with KeyError — LoRA adapter parameters are not in cumem's tag set ([#39934](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/39934))
2. **Adapter-only sync missing**: frameworks must merge LoRA → send full weights → unmerge. Adapter-only sync (send only LoRA delta, load via vLLM's LoRA serving) would eliminate the merge round-trip ([trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975))
3. **LoRA + MoE mismatch**: logprob divergence between training and inference grows with LoRA rank on MoE models (Qwen3.6, GLM-4.7-Flash) ([SkyRL#1776](https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL/issues/1776))

## Downstream demand

- [trl#5975](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/issues/5975): Adapter-only vLLM LoRA sync for GRPO/AsyncGRPO

- [verl#6782](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/issues/6782): Qwen3.5-27B LoRA GRPO — vLLM never emits EOS with rank=64

## Exit criterion

- sleep/wake + LoRA (#39934) no longer crashes

Two weeks from posting.

issues.title: [RFC]: Support ViT Full CUDA Graph (Tracker)
issues.body:
### Motivation.

Multimodal large language models (e.g., Qwen3-VL, Qwen3.5, GLM-V, Kimi K2.5) rely on a Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder to process visual inputs before feeding them into the language model backbone. In production serving scenarios, the ViT forward pass involves launching a large number of small CUDA kernels — including patch embedding, layer normalization, multi-head self-attention, and MLP projections — each of which incurs non-trivial kernel launch overhead on the host side.

Currently, vLLM supports CUDA graph capture for the decoder (LLM) portion of the model, which has proven effective at reducing kernel launch costs and improving throughput. However, the ViT encoder is still executed eagerly, meaning every forward pass re-launches all kernels from scratch. Extending full CUDA graph support to the ViT encoder would allow the entire encoder forward pass to be captured and replayed as a single graph, eliminating per-kernel launch overhead and enabling more consistent, low-latency inference for multimodal models.

issues.title: [Docs] Document NIXL KV connector metrics aggregation semantics
issues.body:
## Summary

The NIXL KV connector logs transfer metrics periodically:

```
KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=4, Avg xfer time (ms)=1.381, P90 xfer time (ms)=2.601, Avg post time (ms)=0.672, P90 post time (ms)=0.801, Avg MB per transfer=2.25, Throughput (MB/s)=1629.549, Avg number of descriptors=72.0
```

Currently there is no documentation explaining what these metrics represent, especially in the context of **multi-rank (TP > 1) deployments**. This has already caused confusion among users.

## Current behavior

All metrics are **aggregated across all TP ranks** before summary stats are computed:

1. Each TP rank independently records per-transfer telemetry (`transfer_duration`, `post_duration`, `bytes_transferred`, `num_descriptors`) via `NixlKVConnectorStats.record_transfer()` in [`stats.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py).
2. Stats from all ranks are concatenated via `aggregate()` (`list.extend()`).
3. `reduce()` computes averages, percentiles, and throughput over the **combined** pool of observations from all ranks.

This means:
- **"Num successful transfers"** is the total count across all ranks, not per-rank.
- **"Avg MB per transfer"** is the average over all individual rank-level transfers, not the total bytes moved for a single KV cache transfer operation.
- **"Throughput (MB/s)"** is `total_MB_all_ranks / total_time_all_ranks` — effectively an average per-rank throughput, not the aggregate system throughput.
- **Percentiles (P90)** are computed over the combined distribution of all ranks' transfer times.

This is unintuitive because users may expect metrics to reflect per-engine totals or aggregate system throughput.

## What needs to be documented

1. **Docstrings in `stats.py`**: Add clear documentation to `NixlKVConnectorStats` explaining that stats are aggregated across all TP ranks and what each metric represents in that context.
2. **Inline comments in `reduce()`**: Clarify the semantics of throughput and averages — that they are per-rank averages over the combined observation pool.
3. **Docstrings in `metrics.py`**: Document the `observe()` → `aggregate()` → `reduce()` → `log()` pipeline and the fact that stats arrive pre-aggregated across workers.
4. **(Optional) Docs page**: Add a section to the disaggregated serving documentation explaining how to interpret the KV Transfer metrics log line.

## Relevant files

- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/stats.py` — `NixlKVConnectorStats` (recording, aggregation, reduction)
- `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/metrics.py` — `KVConnectorLogging` (observe/log pipeline), `KVConnectorStats` (base class)

## Context

See related discussion: metrics are aggregated across ranks rather than reported per-rank or per-engine. This is a deliberate design choice (fire-and-forget from workers), but it needs to be clearly documented so users can correctly interpret the numbers.

issues.title: [Bug]: Wrong timestamps if audio > 30s
issues.body:
### Your current environment


NA

### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Segment level timestamps are incrementally offset by ~0.5s per segment.**

When transcribing long audio with vLLM Whisper, segment-level timestamps are increasingly inaccurate. Chunking uses by default a 1s window to find low-energy (quiet) regions for splitting, so the next chunk may start up to 1s earlier than the nominal chunk length. This offset is not compensated for when generating segment timestamps, resulting in an average delay of ~0.5s per segment, which accumulates (e.g., 5s after 10 segments).

Clients can workaround by subtracting 0.5s per segment, but that's obviously not accurate.

Also, the [related documentation](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/e83b7e379c11bf136c1b96bc6a67b6d2207cfde4/docs/contributing/model/transcription.md#audio-preprocessing-and-chunking) is not correct: there are no overlapping chunks, but just a window for searching the best split point. Maybe this confusion is the cause of the issue.

issues.title: [RFC]: Limit the use of envvars in vLLM
issues.body:
### Motivation.

vLLM's envvars are on the edge of getting out of control. There are many envvars should instead be configs. Like the attention backend, all2all kernel backend, and even there is a flag to control KV cache layout. envvars are evil because:

1. It is equivalent of using global variables everywhere in the code, which is a bad programming practice.
2. envvars have no advanced structure like, hierarchy, typechecks, etc. 

In summary, I think envvars are the kind of thing that is very easy to add so people tend to add envvars as the shortest path to implement their feature, but this can quickly becomes unmanageable and makes the project very hard to use. 

### Proposed Change.

I think we should:

1. Spend some effort on reviewing the current envvars and move many of them to configs.
2. Have very strict bar on what can be an envvar and question every new envvars in vllm.

issues.title: [Feature]: Optimize collectives in TP MoE case using torch.compile pass
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

To avoid redundant work in MoE models in the TP case, sequence parallelism was added to the Deepseek model definition in #24134 and expanded to other models in #24982. However, to avoid performing surgery on the linear layer, the current approach performs more communication than necessary. With a torch.compile custom pass, we can rewrite the graph to remove the redundant computation.

### More details

Before the SP optimization, the ops in the model were:
```
- o_proj:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...] (incomplete results)
- all_reduce:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- rms_norm:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- router:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- experts:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- ...
```

With sequence parallel enabled, this becomes:
```
- o_proj: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...] (incomplete results)
- all_reduce: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- rms_norm:[num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
- chunk: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- router: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- experts: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- all_gather: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
```

Additionally, experts now properly do the dp+tp<->ep dispatch instead of just the original replicated dp<->ep dispatch.

Notice that the `all_reduce` (and `rms_norm`) do redundant communication as each TP rank only requires partial results. With a compile pass, we can convert the `all_reduce` -> `rms_norm` -> `chunk` sequence into a `reduce_scatter` -> `rms_norm`:

```
- o_proj: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...] (incomplete results)
- reduce_scatter: [num_tokens, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- router: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- experts: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens/tp, ...]
- all_gather: [num_tokens/tp, ...] -> [num_tokens, ...]
```

We should create a new `SequenceParallelismMoEPass`, controlled by a new `PassConfig.enable_sp_moe` flag (following the new naming convention in #27995) so that it can be turned on independently of regular SP. We will likely need to pad the number of tokens to a multiple of TP size, although like described in #29136, there are alternatives.

#### SP
Additionally, to make SP-MoE compatible with AsyncTP, the SP pass should also replace the `all_gather` -> `rms_norm` sequence with `rms_norm` -> `all_gather`, such that the `all_gather` can be fused with the following QKV proj. We can see that in the SP case we perform an `all_gather` instead of `all_reduce` after the MLP layer.

### Alternatives

Alternatively, the original optimization could be done as a compile pass as well, which would significantly clean up the MoE model definitions. However, that would mean that `VLLM_COMPILE` compilation mode would be required for this optimization and if compilation is disabled, the optimization would be disabled as well. Generally we accept lower performance in eager mode as compilation is on by default, but I know there was a reason this was done this way (don't remember why).

We could also just let the SP pass first transform `all_reduce` -> `rms_norm` into `reduce_scatter` -> `rms_norm` -> `all_gather` and then eliminate the `all_gather` -> `chunk` combo. But then we have less control over SP after MoE (although it seems like all_reduce is not even used in that case).

### Additional context

Original proposal comment: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/24982#pullrequest

issues.title: Upgrade to Transformers v5
issues.body:
## What is this issue?

This issue serves as a living tracker for the current issues preventing us from upgrading vLLM to Transformers v5.

We will use sub-issues to track individual failures and PRs should be made against these sub-issues.

The solutions to these issues may need to be applied to either:

- Transformers in the form of:
  - Adding missing backward compatibility (usually for custom code models)
  - General bug fixes/improvements to new features of v5
- vLLM in the form of:
  - Forward compatibility with how something is now done in v5
  - Edge case handling for issues that v4 ignored (such as config validation)

Sometimes, the issue is simply with the model checkpoint itself, for example if it:

- Contains a malformed `config.json` that cannot be used to instantiate the newly input validated `PreTrainedConfig` class
- Custom code* uses deprecated/removed APIs

In these situations, the best solution will likely be to skip these tests in vLLM and open a PR to Transformers to contribute this model. This will be faster and more sustainable than waiting for the model vendor to fix their custom model code, sometimes they nevert do.

Contributing the new model should be done using the new [Modular Transformers](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/modular_transformers) so that the implementation is easy to maintain and will remain maintained by the Transformers team.

issues.title: [Feature]: `CustomOp` cleanup
issues.body:
### 🚀 Motivation

Currently, we do not have a consistent plan for "light" custom ops (subclasses of `CustomOp` with both torch-native and GPU implementations). As we work on improved performance on NVIDIA Blackwell and AMD, we should be more intentional with CompilationConfig defaults that control custom op dispatching. This is a parent issue that tracks smaller PRs addressing `CustomOp`s.

In vLLM, there are two kinds of custom kernels/ops:
1. "heavy" ops like GEMMs, MoE, and attention, which will mostly use tuned custom kernels for maximum performance.
2. "light" ops like `RMSNorm`, `SiluAndMul`, and `RoPE`, which have both torch-native and custom GPU implementations.

This issue only refers to "light" ops, which are (or should be) all subclasses of `CustomOp`.

When we enabled `torch.compile` by default in V1, the plan was to reduce our reliance on custom kernels to reduce maintenance costs and code complexity, even with minor performance costs. Recent versions of `torch` actually produce Triton kernels faster than our custom op implementations anyway.

However, with startup time concerns (#19824), it seems like we want good performance even with Inductor disabled (more discussion on startup times to come in a follow-up issue). Additionally, custom op performance has been reported to be better than torch.compile-generated Triton kernels on AMD.

### ❗ Issues

This is a list of current issues with custom ops. The following section tracks proposed and WIP solutions. Larger line items might have their own issue or get one in the future.

1. [Perf] FP8 quantization not fused with rms_norm/silu_mul (because fp8 quant doesn't have a torch native implementation)
2. [Perf] AMD uses custom ops but fusion for them is hardcoded to disabled.
3. [Perf] We don't have good visibility into performance differences between GPU and torch native implementations of custom ops across different models and hardware platforms.
4. [Perf][Code Quality] Fused and unfused custom ops currently reimplement the same code, and only some are vectorized.
5. [Testing] Custom op tests either don't exist or reimplement Torch naive implementations
6. [Compilation] Current custom passes rely on custom op pattern matching, which involves auto-functionalization (#14703) and requires custom ops to be enabled. If custom ops are slower than native impls, that means e.g. attention+quant fusion needs to take a hit on other quants to fuse the o-proj one. I'll create an RFC for this.

### ✅  Solutions

Once we have benchmarking numbers, we can set sensible defaults. Improving startup time will likely result in more explicit "profiles" with better config defaults.

Detailed solution tracking:

1. ✅ @ProExpertProg: FP8 `CustomOp`s in #19830
2. ✅ #19181 removed hardcoded `enable_fusion=False`.
3. 🚧 WIP @gshtras and @SageMoore are collecting some benchmarking numbers for custom op performance. More benchmarking can be done as needed. Automating some of this would be great as well.
4. ❗ TODO consolidating, vectorizing and cleaning up CUDA/HIP implementations of custom ops.
5. ❗ TODO add testing utilities for custom ops.
6. ✅ match and perform fusion with custom ops disabled: #24604

#### ➕ Other potential improvements

- [ ] Simplify custom op enablement
- [ ] Improve custom op documentation
- [ ] Custom op microbenchmarks

issues.title: [Transformers v5] InternVL2
issues.body:
This is a sub-issue forming part of the work in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/38379, please read the description of this issue before beginning to work on this one.

## Which test is failing?

Transformers v5 creates the model on the meta device first, then loads the weights, similarly to what vLLM does. The issue here is that the custom model code in the checkpoint tries to use real tensors as part of model structure construction.

Since the issue here is with the HF reference generation, this cannot be fixed in vLLM (other than skipping the tests until the model works with Transformers v5). The proper solution to this issue is to upstream this architecture, which shouldn't be too hard using Modular Transformers as the text backbone is Qwen2 so that can be reused.

```console
$ pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_common.py::test_single_image_models[intern_vl-test_case25]
...
RuntimeError: Tensor.item() cannot be called on meta tensors
```

## How to configure my environment?

It's very important that you install both vLLM and Transformers from source so that your test results reflect the current state of both libraries.

```console
# Or your fork
git clone https://github.com/huggingface/transformers.git
git clone https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm.git

cd vllm
VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 uv pip install -e .
uv pip install -e ../transformers
```

issues.title: [Bug]: ModelOpt Llama-4 Checkpoints Take 5+ minutes to load
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

In working on some MoE refactors, I discovered that L4 for ModelOpt takes 5+minutes to load weights even from CPU page cache. 
- https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-FP8

The root cause is basically this hack logic to load the state dict that ModelOpt uses
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/models/llama4.py#L439-L523 [modelopt is the fused case] 

What happens is that the CPU tensor (loaded weight) that we are going to load into the GPU tensor (param) becomes non-contiguous due to this logic. As a result, when we eventually call `_copy()` from CPU->GPU we are calling this on a non-contiguous cpu tensor which takes 3-4s per weight.

To hack around this for local R&D, I simply immediately move the loaded_weight to the GPU. This makes the gather happen on the GPU which accelerates things a lot. This isn't reasonable as an actual solution though

We should investigate where the logic in the weight loader can avoid creating non-contiguous CPU tensors

issues.title: [torch.compile] E2E correctness testing for fusions
issues.body:
E2E tests for fusions (`tests/compile/fusions_e2e`) have done a great job preventing fusion regressions where model/forward code changes break a custom torch.compile fusion pass. However, we currently have no way of testing correctness for these fusion configurations.

It would be good to investigate an approach where we only run a few layers of a model and compare the outputs. This would be helpful for correctness testing in general, and we could compare the outputs to both a baseline vLLM configuration and the huggingface baseline.

This would likely require some work to fix weight loading for models like DeepSeek when `--hf-overrides.num_hidden_layers` is overriden.

issues.title: [Feature]: Priority scheduling supports preemption of requests in the running queue by requests in the waiting queue
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

The current priority scheduling only supports evicting low-priority requests from the running queue when resources are insufficient. However, when scheduling the waiting queue, if pending requests cannot be scheduled (for example, when the number of requests in the running queue has reached max_num_seqs), even high-priority requests cannot preempt requests in the running queue.

tasks.why_core: 参与核心 Attention API 的语义定义，提升框架在极端边界条件下的鲁棒性。
tasks.goal: 在 Python 层的 Attention API 中拦截 `kv_len == 0` 的情况，直接返回全 0 的 output 和 `-inf` 的 LSE，避免调用底层 Kernel 导致未定义行为。

positioning.overview:
FlashInfer 是一个专为 LLM 推理服务设计的高性能 GPU 算子库，提供 Attention、GEMM 和 MoE 的统一 API。对于你这样具备 CuTe/CUTLASS 和底层优化经验的资深 Kernel 工程师来说，这是一个极具价值的切入点：它不仅向下封装了 FlashAttention-2/3、cuDNN、CUTLASS 等后端，还原生支持从 Turing (SM75) 到最新的 Blackwell (SM100/120) 架构。项目目前处于核心功能高度成熟（被 vLLM、SGLang 等头部框架作为底层依赖），但前沿架构（如 Blackwell NVFP4、SM90+ CuTe-DSL MoE）处于高频迭代的阶段。

**针对你的硬约束（仅有 Mac + Colab T4）的残酷现实**：
FlashInfer 强依赖 CUDA 环境，且默认采用 JIT（Just-In-Time）编译机制（见 `CLAUDE.md` 和 `flashinfer/aot.py`）。这意味着你在 Apple Silicon 上**无法进行任何本地编译和算子验证**。你的 Colab T4 (SM75) 只能用于验证最基础的 Turing 架构算子，而你擅长的 CuTe/CUTLASS（通常针对 SM80+）、FP8/FP4 量化（SM89/SM90/SM100）以及最新的 MoE 优化，在 T4 上完全无法运行。如果你要切入本项目，你只能在 Mac 上通过 `.devcontainer` 或 Docker 配置 C++ LSP 进行“盲写”和静态分析，强依赖项目的 CI 系统（Jenkins/GitHub Actions）进行正确性验证，或者专注于 Python 层的 JIT 调度逻辑、算子融合的图层优化（PyTorch 侧）以及端侧部署相关的上层封装。
positioning.problem: 解决 LLM 推理场景下特有的性能瓶颈：动态 Batching 导致的内存碎片化（通过 Paged/Ragged KV-Cache 解决）、Prefill 与 Decode 阶段的计算特征差异、MoE 模型的复杂路由开销，以及极低延迟要求下的量化计算（FP8/FP4）和算子融合问题。
positioning.users: 主要目标用户是 LLM 推理框架的开发者（如 vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, MLC-LLM 的核心维护者），以及需要为特定模型（如 DeepSeek MLA、Llama-4 MoE）定制高性能推理后端的 AI 性能工程师。

landscape.difference: FlashAttention 侧重于模型训练（Forward/Backward）和标准 Attention；FlashInfer 专精于推理，提供 Paged KV-Cache、Decode、Append、Cascade 等推理特有算子，并扩展到了 MoE 和 GEMM 领域。
它们是 FlashInfer 的上游使用者。FlashInfer 作为底层的 Kernel Provider，将复杂的 CUDA/CuTe 算子封装为 PyTorch API，使得这些服务框架无需为每种新 GPU 架构手写底层算子。
CUTLASS 是 NVIDIA 提供的底层 C++ 模板库。FlashInfer 将 CUTLASS（及 CuTe）作为核心依赖（见 `3rdparty/cutlass`），在其之上构建了适用于动态形状和特定 LLM 负载的 JIT 编译算子。

positioning.stage: 核心功能 Production-Ready（已被广泛集成），前沿硬件支持（Blackwell, NVFP4, CuTe-DSL）处于 Experimental/WIP 阶段。

capabilities.capability: Paged & Ragged KV-Cache Attention
DeepSeek MLA (Multi-Latent Attention)
Fused MoE & Routing
CuTe-DSL Integration
NVFP4 / MXFP4 Quantization
JIT Compilation & Caching
Multi-GPU Communication (AllReduce/MNNVL)
Sorting-Free Sampling (Top-K/Top-P)

stack: Jinja (用于算子代码模板生成)
positioning.numbers: 仓库规模庞大，C++ 核心代码位于 `csrc/` 包含 3133 个文件，Python 接口 `flashinfer/` 包含 1254 个文件，测试用例 `tests/` 达 432 个。近期发布了 v0.7.0rc3 和 v0.6.18 版本。提交极为频繁，最近的热点集中在 `csrc/kda` (59次)、`csrc/gdn` (58次) 和 `flashinfer/moe_ep` (23次)，显示出对新架构算子和 MoE 的高强度开发。

codemap.layers: FlashInfer 的架构设计呈现出极其清晰的自顶向下分层，这对于只能依赖 Mac 进行静态分析和 Python 层开发的你来说是个好消息。第一层是【Python 接口与调度层】（位于 flashinfer/ 目录），这里是用户入口，负责处理 PyTorch Tensor、管理 JIT/AOT 编译缓存（flashinfer-jit-cache）、解析环境变量（如 FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS），并根据启发式规则或 Autotuner 将请求路由到合适的后端（如 cuDNN、CUTLASS 或原生 Kernel）。由于这一层完全是 Python 代码，你可以在 Mac 上无缝进行图层融合、调度策略优化和 JIT 逻辑的开发。第二层是【C++ 绑定与图层】（位于 csrc/ 目录），通过 TVM FFI（tvm_ffi_utils.h）将 C++ 暴露给 Python。这一层的核心特征是“Plan & Run”模式（如 BatchPagedAttentionPlan），在 CPU 上计算 Workspace 大小、处理 Indptr 数组，并支持 CUDA Graph 捕获。你可以在 Mac 上通过 C++ LSP 静态分析这部分逻辑。第三层是【核心 Kernel 层】（位于 include/flashinfer/），这是纯粹的、框架无关的 CUDA 模板代码，实现了从 Turing 到 Blackwell 的底层算子。第四层是【实验性与前沿架构层】（位于 csrc/blackwell_* 和 csrc/cake_*），包含大量由 Cake 生成的、针对 SM100/103 的 NVFP4/MXFP4 汇编级优化代码（涉及 TMA 描述符和 mbarrier）。对于后两层，由于你没有 SM80+ GPU，你只能进行“盲写”，强依赖项目的 CI 系统和代码审查（CONTRIBUTING.md 中明确了实验性特性的严格 Review 流程）来验证正确性。

modules.role: 提供 PyTorch 用户接口，管理 JIT 编译缓存，执行后端路由（Stable vs Experimental）。
modules.notes: Mac 友好的开发区域。包含大量调度逻辑和实验性后端的入口（@flashinfer_experimental_api）。

modules.notes: 使用 TVM FFI 导出。包含大量针对不同架构的绑定代码（如 batch_mla_sm90_binding.cu）。

modules.notes: 必须在 GPU 上验证。包含 CuTe/CUTLASS 的底层调用。

modules.notes: 近期热点（23次提交）。针对 SM90 进行了深度优化（MoeShrinkKernelConfig）。

modules.role: 针对 SM100/103 架构的极致优化，包含 NVFP4/MXFP4 和 TMA/mbarrier 汇编级实现。
